minutes.headline: Parks Commission set two April public sessions on Marshall Park borrowing and reviewed plans for the spring fair.
minutes.summary: The commission heard facilities and recreation updates, including beach staffing and hours, then a long presentation on the planned town fair. It reviewed bond counsel's tax-impact scenarios for the full and phase-one Marshall Park projects and chose tentative dates for two public information sessions, with the location to be confirmed. The only formal vote approved the January and February minutes with a name correction.

attendees.role: presenter, Lunenburg Business Association, attended by Zoom

votes.motion: Approve the January 15th and February 19th minutes, correcting 'A Shapiro' to 'C Shapiro'.

budget_items.topic: Facilities and revolving account financial sheets
budget_items.what_was_said: Financial sheets for the facilities and revolving accounts were handed out. Nothing has been billed against them yet this season.
The full project cost was given from bond counsel's information.
The phase one project plus the pavilion building was costed separately.
Bond counsel's 18-year scenario shows an annual impact on the average single family house.
The phase one scenario over 18 years was given per household.
The finance director may require a 15-year term for phase one only. This was left to be confirmed.
Staff are gathering fee information from other towns. The item was pushed to April.
The recreation director said she has limited weekly hours to build programs.

decisions.decision: Tentative dates set for two public information sessions on Marshall Park: Thursday April 10 at 7 p.m. and Saturday April 26 at 10 a.m., location to be determined.
The evening session was discussed as moving to Wednesday April 9, with TCP as the likely location. The recreation director is to confirm availability the next day.
The Marshall Park memorial area request will be raised at the next design team meeting.
The user fees item was pushed to the April meeting and is to be retitled 'park user fees'.
The April public sessions will be posted as commission meetings, possibly with an agenda, so no separate regular April meeting is planned.
The chair asked for a volunteer to be chair after the election, with no answer required that night. The item was left for a later meeting.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission tentatively set two public information sessions on Marshall Park for Thursday April 10 at 7 p.m. and Saturday April 26 at 10 a.m.
The evening session was discussed as moving to Wednesday April 9, likely at TCP; the recreation director is to confirm availability the next day.
Members reviewed bond counsel's 18-year tax-impact scenarios for the full Marshall Park project and for phase one, each given per household.
The finance director may require a 15-year debt exclusion term for phase one only; this was left to be confirmed.
Park user fees were pushed to the April meeting to be retitled 'park user fees', while staff gather fee information from other towns.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park borrowing would be repaid through property taxes, so the public sessions are where residents can hear the per-household impact before any vote on the debt.
The debt term (18 years versus a possible 15 for phase one) changes the size of the annual charge on a tax bill, and it was still unconfirmed at this meeting.
